summary: Source pass applying the lead-only host rule adopted on 2026-10-23: encyclopedias, newsletters, advocacy groups and advocacy trackers, association and trade-group summaries, general aggregators and litigants' own pages are leads, never sources. 109 records were touched: 82 reviewed in full (a research pass found replacement primary documents or reputable news reports for the facts those hosts had carried, then an independent review built each final record) and 27 handled mechanically (unused lead-only summary sources removed, nothing else changed). Across the 109 records, 122 sources were removed and 157 added (agency releases, Federal Register and govinfo documents, court orders on CourtListener, wire and trade press); 51 timeline events were re-sourced to a replacement that states the same fact; 20 events whose only support was a lead-only summary were removed, with the fact kept in uncertainties as an unverified lead that names the host; 13 scanned copies of official documents on such hosts were kept and retitled as third-party copies. Encyclopedia-derived sentences in 28 records were either re-sourced or reworded as unverified leads at low confidence pending official documentation. No stage or progress value changed. Confidence changed on eight records: c00-09 80 to 78, c05-07 76 to 74, c09-18 50 to 46, c12-13 80 to 79, c19-02 82 to 79 and c19-06 80 to 79 (replacement sources are secondary or a lead-only fact now sits in uncertainties), c12-10 68 to 78 (the restated statutory schedule was confirmed on an official text) and c19-22 70 to 72. Court status corrected on three records from the court dockets opened during the pass: c00-09 from enjoined to pending (a status report is due under the 2026-10-07 order), c05-07 from vacated to enjoined, c18-10 from dismissed to pending. Think tanks and research institutions, trade press and law firms are not covered by the rule and were left in place. Counts unchanged at 627. Export to GitHub in this run.
title: Lead-only hosts pass, 2026-10-23
